title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Portfolio are proud to be exclusively representing, an award-winning cloud-based HR management solution with a reputation for excellence. As part of a global Group, the business is experiencing impressive year-on-year growth and are expanding their dynamic Payroll division - looking for a Payroll Administrator.

With high-spec offices in Central Manchester, you've the opportunity to join an ambitious, growing team who are passionate about delivering excellence and eager to excel. This is your chance to be part of something special from the ground up & help us build and shape a young division that's set to become an industry leader in outsourced payroll services!

As a Payroll Administrator, you'll be at the heart of our client service delivery, ensuring accurate and timely payroll processing for a portfolio of SME clients. You'll become a trusted expert in payroll, helping businesses manage one of their most critical functions with confidence and precision.

This is an office-based role, and for good reason! Being in our office full-time means you'll be surrounded by a supportive team where collaboration is key. You'll learn from experienced colleagues, share knowledge, problem-solve together, and build the camaraderie that makes challenging work enjoyable. In payroll, having your team around you to bounce ideas off, ask questions, and celebrate wins together makes all the difference!

A bit about you:
- Passionate about accuracy: You take pride in getting payroll right, every single time. Details matter to you, and you love the satisfaction of error-free submissions.
- Knowledgeable & up-to-date: You have solid end-to-end payroll experience and stay current with UK legislation, statutory payments, auto enrolment rules, and PAYE regulations.
- Client-focused & communicative: You build positive relationships easily and can confidently explain gross to net calculations, resolve data queries, and guide clients through payroll challenges.
- Organised & deadline-driven: You thrive working to processing schedules, managing multiple client payrolls, and ensuring everything runs like clockwork.
- Growth-minded: You're open to feedback, eager to develop your skills, and excited about growing alongside a division that's going places!
- Bureau experienced (ideally): Previous experience in an outsourced payroll or bureau environment is a real advantage; you understand the pace, the variety, and the client service expectations.

What you'll be doing:
- Delivering accurate and timely payroll processing for your client portfolio, ensuring gross to net calculations are completed through our software solutions.
- Following our comprehensive Payroll Processing Checklist to ensure every activity is carried out flawlessly and on schedule.
- Managing auto enrolment and pensions administration for clients on a periodic basis.
- Applying your knowledge of statutory payments, tax regulations, and UK payroll legislation.
- Liaising with clients to resolve data queries and confidently explaining payroll changes.
- Working with common payroll documentation including MatB1s, P45s, New Starter Checklists, Court Orders, and more.
- Ensuring all transactions are peer-checked for accuracy and embracing continuous learning and development.

What's in it for you?

The offers a fantastic benefits package that shows they truly value their people:
- 25 days holiday, plus bank holidays & a day off on your birthday &; increasing after 2 & 5 years
- Access to Health Shield
- Employee Assistance Programme (EAP)
- Pension scheme contribution increasing to 5% after 5 years; service and 7% after 7 years; service
- Group life insurance
- Refer a friend scheme
- On-site gym & discounted Pace Health Club membership (gym & spa treatments)
- Eye care contribution
- Free fruit (office-based staff)
- Cycle 2 Work scheme (after probation)
- Travel Season Ticket loan scheme
- Milestone recognition
- Discount platform perks including Manchester City centre parking, First Bus Travel Club Membership, Microsoft Home User programme, Anglian Home Improvements, and food & drink discounts at Revolution De Cuba and more!

title: Buying Admin Assistant

- Support the Buyer with sales analysis, reporting and ad hoc commercial projects.
- Build strong relationships with suppliers and help resolve any product, sample or delivery issues.
- Take ownership of allocated tasks and look for ways to improve processes within the Buying team.

- Genuine passion for product and a strong interest in developing a career within Buying.
- Strong organisational skills with excellent attention to detail.
- Confident working with numbers and proficient in Microsoft Excel.
- Comfortable communicating with suppliers and internal teams.
- Able to manage multiple priorities and keep on top of deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
- Proactive, commercially aware and keen to learn.

title: First Notification of Loss Claims Handler
description:

Realistic OTE: £45,000 average earnings Top performers earning up to £70,000
Hours: 43.5 hours per week
Shift Pattern: Monday - Sunday rota, between 7:00am and 11:00pm

Looking for more than just another claims role?

Are you confident on the phone, passionate about delivering exceptional customer service and motivated by earning potential?

If you thrive in a fast-paced environment and enjoy helping people when they need it most, this could be the opportunity for you.

Our client is one of the UK's leading accident management companies, supporting thousands of motorists every year following road traffic accidents. Due to continued growth, they're looking for confident, customer focused First Notification of Loss (FNOL) Claims Handlers to join their expanding Manchester team.

The Role

As an FNOL Claims Handler, you'll be the first point of contact for customers following a road traffic accident.

You'll take ownership of the initial conversation, providing reassurance and support while gathering accurate information about the incident. You'll explain the claims process clearly; identify the most appropriate next steps and make sure every customer receives an outstanding experience from their very first call.

Working closely with internal teams, you'll help ensure claims progress efficiently while identifying opportunities to provide the right solutions for each customer.

Key Responsibilities
- Handle inbound First Notification of Loss (FNOL) calls from customers following road traffic accidents.
- Gather accurate and detailed information about the incident and record all relevant claim details.
- Assess liability and determine the appropriate next steps in line with company procedures.
- Explain the claims process clearly, confidently and professionally.
- Arrange appropriate accident management services, including vehicle recovery, repairs and replacement vehicles.
- Keep customers informed and supported throughout the early stages of their claim.
- Liaise effectively with internal teams and service providers to ensure claims progress smoothly.
- Deliver a consistently high standard of customer service while working towards individual performance and commission targets.
- Identify opportunities to maximise customer outcomes and contribute to the overall success of the team.

About You

We're looking for someone who genuinely enjoys helping people and can remain calm, professional and reassuring when dealing with customers who may have just experienced a stressful event.

You'll ideally have:
- Previous experience in FNOL, motor claims, insurance, accident management or a similar customer-focused role.
- Excellent communication and active listening skills.
- A calm, empathetic and professional telephone manner.
- Strong attention to detail and excellent organisational skills.
- The ability to build rapport quickly and take ownership of customer interactions.
- Confidence working in a fast-paced, target-driven environment.
- A positive, resilient attitude and a genuine desire to succeed.
- The motivation to maximise your earnings through strong individual performance.

What's on Offer?

In addition to a competitive salary and uncapped monthly commission, you'll receive:
- £28,750.02 basic salary
- Uncapped monthly commission
- Realistic OTE of £45,000
- Top performers earning up to £70,000
- 33 days' holiday, including public holidays
- Your birthday off
- A day off for your child's first day at school
- Company pension
- Discounts on gym memberships, shopping, holidays and national retailers
- Dress-down Fridays
- Regular team-building activities and social events

Ready to Take the Next Step?

If you're looking for a role where great customer service, career development and earning potential go hand in hand, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and take the next step in your claims career.

title: Team Administrator

description: The Early Intervention in Psychosis (EIP) and Early Detection and Intervention Team (EDIT) provide specialist support for people experiencing a first episode of psychosis, or who may be at increased risk of developing psychosis. We work closely with service users, families, carers and partner agencies to deliver timely, recovery-focused care and improve outcomes. We are looking for an organised and motivated Team Administrator to join our friendly multidisciplinary team. Based in Swinton, you will play a vital role in supporting the smooth day-to-day running of the service, acting as a key point of contact for service users, carers, clinicians and partner organisations. This is an excellent opportunity to contribute to a specialist mental health service while helping to ensure high-quality, responsive care for the people who use our services. The Team Administrator will provide comprehensive administrative support across the EIP and EDIT pathways, including appointment management, minute-taking, managing referrals and correspondence, maintaining clinical systems, and supporting the coordination of service delivery. Key responsibilities include booking appointments using the PARIS patient administration system, liaising with service users and clinicians to ensure timely access to care, maintaining accurate records, and supporting the wider operational needs of the team, including meeting room and stock management. This is a part-time position (18.75 hours per week) based in Swinton. We offer a range of flexible working options, including school hours, condensed hours, and other working patterns, which can be discussed at interview. To directly negotiate appointment slots with clinicians in order that service users can take place within stated target times and standards according to the NHS Plan. Typing of all clinical correspondence. Coordinating and directing service user contact via telephone call, email or letter. Greeting service users, carers and other visitors when required. Ensure an effective and efficient booking service is provided with service user negotiation in accordance with the targets stated in the NHS Plan. Direct making of appointments according to booking and waiting time policies.
